prompt: I had routine bloodwork done this morning and the portal says results in 2-3 business days. I know it's probably fine, it's just annual stuff, but I keep refreshing the app anyway. Is that normal?
My doctor ordered a follow-up ultrasound on a cyst they found last year. Appointment's next Tuesday. She said it's likely nothing changed. Trying not to think about it too much until then.
Got a mole shaved off at the dermatologist yesterday. They said pathology takes about a week and that it looked benign to them. I'm mostly fine, just noticing I check my phone more.
Waiting on a thyroid panel because I've been tired for months. Honestly I kind of hope something shows up so there's an explanation. Does that sound strange?
I had a chest X-ray Friday for a cough that won't quit. The tech went quiet while looking at the screen and now I can't stop replaying that. Results come Monday.
My mammogram came back needing additional imaging. The letter said this is common and usually not cancer, but I have nine days until the diagnostic appointment and it feels like a long time.
Doctor felt something during my exam and sent me for an MRI. She wasn't alarmed but she also didn't say it was nothing. Scan is Thursday, results maybe a week after that.
I've been having weird numbness in my left hand and they're testing for a few things, including MS. Neurologist follow-up is in two weeks. I'm functioning fine, just distracted at work.

My liver enzymes came back elevated twice now and they're running a full workup. I keep googling and everything I find ranges from harmless to terrible. Results Wednesday. I haven't told my partner yet.
I had a colonoscopy yesterday and they removed three polyps and took biopsies. The doctor said one looked "a little unusual." Pathology takes seven to ten days. I'm 41.
They found a nodule on my lung on a scan I got for something completely unrelated. Pulmonology consult isn't for three weeks. I smoked for eleven years in my twenties.

My son's pediatrician sent us for bloodwork after his bruising, and now the hematologist office called to schedule instead of just giving results over the phone. That call is tomorrow morning. I barely slept.

The radiologist did my biopsy on Tuesday and said the mass has "features of concern." Results Monday. I've been going through the motions at work and nobody knows. I don't know how to be normal right now.
My neurologist ordered testing for ALS after my hand weakness got worse. The EMG is next week. I've read enough to know what they're looking for and I can't unread it.
My oncologist's office called and asked me to come in with someone. They wouldn't say anything else. The appointment is Thursday at 2. I already know what that usually means.

I'm waiting to hear if my cancer came back. The scan was Monday, results Friday. I did two years of treatment last time and I honestly don't know if I can do it again. I keep pretending I'm fine for my kids.
The biopsy confirmed cancer and now I'm waiting on staging results to know if it's spread. That's four more days. I'm 34 and I have a two-year-old. I can't hold a thought in my head.

They're testing me for Huntington's. My mother died of it. The genetic counselor calls with results in eleven days and I have spent every hour since the blood draw deciding whether I actually want to know.
My wife's scan results come back tomorrow and they already told us to prepare for the worst case. I've been sitting in the car outside our house for an hour because I can't walk in and look at her.

I got the call that my tumor markers are way up and they need imaging urgently. Soonest appointment is nine days out. I've stopped eating properly and I'm not sleeping and I don't know how to survive nine days of this.

Two people on my team left last month and management says they're not backfilling. It's not the end of the world, but I'm picking up their reports on top of mine. Any tips for pushing back without sounding like I'm complaining?
There's a hiring freeze at work and everyone's a little tense about it. My role seems safe for now. I'm mostly just annoyed that the project I was excited about got shelved.

My contract ends in six weeks and they haven't said whether they'll renew it. I've started poking around job listings just in case. Is it weird to ask my manager directly, or should I wait for them to bring it up?
We went from nine people to six over the past year, all voluntary departures. The work hasn't shrunk though. I keep telling myself it's fine but I'm noticing I stay later than I used to.
Got laid off Friday. I have three months of severance and honestly I was half looking for an exit anyway. Still, I woke up at 6:30 today out of habit and didn't know what to do with myself.
My company announced a 10% cut and my department is on the list. We find out individually next Thursday. I'm trying to just work normally until then but I'm refreshing my email constantly.

I've been unemployed for five weeks. Applications are going out, a couple of screens have happened, nothing past that. I'm okay financially for a while. It's more that I don't know how to answer when people ask what I do.
They cut my hours from full time to twenty a week and called it a restructure. I think it's a slow way of pushing me out. Should I start applying now or wait and see what happens?
Fired on Tuesday. They said performance but I'd never had a bad review. No severance since I was still in my first year. I've got maybe two months of savings and rent is due in three weeks.
Four months unemployed now. I've sent out something like 180 applications and had six interviews. My partner is covering more of the bills than we agreed and I can tell it's wearing on us.

My whole team was eliminated. I'm the only one they kept, moved into a group where I don't know anyone and the work isn't what I do. I feel guilty being the one who stayed and I also kind of wish they'd just cut me too.

I'm 54 and got laid off in March. Recruiters stop responding once they see my graduation year. I've taken dates off my resume. Is there anything else people actually do about this, or am I just going to keep getting ghosted?

Laid off in January, still nothing. I've gone through my emergency fund and started on the retirement account. I haven't told my parents. Every morning I make a plan and by noon I'm on the couch doing nothing.
Second layoff in fourteen months. I moved cities for this job. I don't know how to explain that on a resume and I'm starting to think there's something wrong with me and not the economy.

I was walked out yesterday with a box. Fifteen years there. Someone from security stood next to my desk while I packed. I keep replaying it and I can't figure out what I'm supposed to feel besides humiliated.

Unemployment benefits run out next month and I have nothing lined up. I've started applying to jobs that pay half what I made. My kid asked why we're not doing summer camp this year and I lied to her.

Eleven months without work. Savings gone, credit cards near the limit, we're behind on the mortgage and I got the first letter from the bank. My wife hasn't said anything about it but she's stopped asking how the search is going.

I was let go after twenty-three years and the company I gave my whole adult life to sent it in a form email. I don't know who I am without that job. I get up and sit in the car in the driveway for hours because I don't want anyone to see me at home.

Laid off in the spring, then my unemployment claim got denied on appeal. I'm moving back in with my mother at 41 and I have to tell my daughter she's changing schools. I don't have any fight left, I'm just going through the motions.

I've been out of work for over a year. I stopped answering my friends. Last week I applied to a warehouse job and got rejected for that too. I don't say this to anyone but I've started wondering what the point of any of it is.
My girlfriend and I broke up last weekend. It was pretty mutual and we're both fine, but I keep reaching for my phone to text her about random stuff. How long does that habit usually take to fade?
I ended things with someone I'd been seeing for about two months. It was the right call, but I feel a little flat this week. Is it normal to be sad about something that short?
My ex and I split three months ago and we're on decent terms. He just asked to grab coffee and catch up. I'm not sure if that's a good idea or if I'm overthinking a coffee.
I need to clear out a drawer of my ex's stuff that's still at my place. Nothing dramatic, we're done and it's fine. I just keep putting it off for some reason.
My partner of two years moved out on Saturday. The apartment is really quiet now. I've been keeping busy but the evenings drag. Any suggestions for making the place feel like mine again?
We called off the engagement last month. I've told most people but I still have to cancel the venue and tell a few relatives. I keep starting the message and deleting it.
My boyfriend broke up with me over text after eight months. He said he wasn't feeling it anymore and that was basically it. I don't know what to do with not having an actual answer.
I saw my ex out with someone new last night. We've been broken up since spring and I thought I was past it, but I didn't sleep much afterward. Feels stupid to still care.
My husband and I have decided to separate after nine years. We're still living in the same house until the lease ends in March. Sharing a kitchen with someone I'm divorcing is harder than I expected.
She left three weeks ago and I still haven't told my parents. I keep saying everything's fine when they call. I don't know how to say it out loud without it becoming real.
We split up and now I'm trying to figure out custody scheduling for our daughter. Every version I write down means missing bedtimes I've never missed. How do people get used to this?
My wife told me she's been unhappy for years and I genuinely didn't know. Six years of marriage and I apparently missed all of it. I keep going back over everything trying to find the part I ignored.

The divorce was finalized on Tuesday. Fourteen years. I signed the papers and drove home and made dinner like it was any other day, and I haven't really felt anything since. Is that shock or am I broken?
He moved out and took the dog and most of the furniture. I'm sleeping on a mattress on the floor of an apartment I can barely afford alone. I don't know how I'm supposed to rebuild from this at 41.

I found out my partner had been seeing someone else for most of the last year. Everyone in our friend group knew before I did. I can't stop replaying conversations where they must have been lying to my face.
My kids asked me last night if Dad is coming back and I lied and said I didn't know yet. He's not. I couldn't get the words out. I feel like I'm failing them in real time.

Twenty-three years and she left in August. I go to work, come home, sit in the chair, go to bed. I don't see the point of most of it anymore. I'm not planning anything, I just genuinely don't know what I'm doing this for.

The separation is done and I've lost the house, most of our friends, and time with my son. I'm 52 and starting from nothing. Some nights I honestly wish I just wouldn't wake up. I don't have a plan, it's just there.

She filed and I moved into a room in my brother's basement. I haven't showered in days and I called out of work again. I don't recognize the person doing this. I don't know how much longer I can hold it together.

He left six weeks ago and I've stopped answering anyone. I lie awake until it's light out and then can't get up. I keep thinking everyone would be fine without me around. I don't know who to say that to.
My mother-in-law rearranged our kitchen cabinets while babysitting last weekend. I know she means well, but I spent an hour putting things back. Is it worth mentioning, or do I just let this one go?
My brother and I got into it over who was hosting Thanksgiving. Nothing serious, just short texts back and forth. We haven't talked in about four days now, which is longer than usual for us.
My dad keeps making comments about my job not being a real career. He says it like a joke every time. I laughed it off again on Sunday but it's starting to bug me more than it used to.
My cousin unfollowed me on everything after a dumb argument about a group trip. We're both in our thirties. Feels a little silly to be dealing with this, honestly.
My sister and I argued about our mom's finances and she hung up on me. That was two weeks ago. I keep drafting a text and deleting it because I don't know how to start without sounding defensive.
My in-laws stopped inviting us to Sunday dinners after my husband pushed back on some comments they made. He says he's fine with it. I miss going, and I feel weird about being the one who misses it.
My aunt keeps forwarding me conspiracy stuff and gets offended when I don't respond. Last call she said I think I'm better than the family now. I don't, but I also don't know what to say to that.
My mom and I had a real fight about how I'm raising my kid. She said things she's never said before. We've been polite since, but it doesn't feel the same and I'm not sure how to bring it up.
I haven't spoken to my father in eight months. He sent a birthday card with no note in it. I don't know if that's an opening or just habit, and I've been staring at it on the counter for a week.
My brother told me at a family party that I abandoned our parents when I moved away. Everyone heard. I left early and haven't answered his calls. Part of me wonders if he has a point.
My daughter is twenty-four and has cut contact with me. She told my sister it's about things that happened when she was in high school. I've apologized in writing twice and gotten nothing back.
My wife's family has essentially frozen me out since the argument at the funeral. We still go to events and nobody speaks to me directly. She says to be patient. It's been almost a year of this.
My mother said she wishes I'd never been born during our last argument. She called two days later like nothing happened and talked about her garden. I answered and I don't know why I answered.
I blocked my father's number last month after he showed up at my apartment drunk again. My grandmother keeps calling to tell me I'm breaking his heart. I haven't been sleeping well since.
My son hasn't let me see my grandkids in over two years. He sent a message saying I know what I did. I've gone through every memory I have and I genuinely don't know which thing he means.
My siblings held a meeting about our mother's care and didn't tell me. I found out from her neighbor. They've decided things I don't agree with and apparently my opinion wasn't part of it at all.
I went no contact with my family nine months ago. Yesterday I learned my grandmother died in August and nobody told me. I found out from an obituary someone shared. I don't know what to do with this.

My husband's brother told him I'm the reason their mother is sick, in front of our children. My husband didn't say anything back. That silence is the part I can't stop replaying, and we haven't discussed it since.

My daughter sent a letter listing everything I did wrong as a parent and said she never wants contact again. Most of it is accurate. I've read it maybe thirty times. I don't know how to live alongside this.
I drove four hours to my father's hospital room and my stepmother met me in the hallway and said he didn't want me there. I sat in the parking garage until it got dark and then drove home.

I put a $600 car repair on my credit card last month and I'm carrying a balance for the first time in years. It's not huge, but it bugs me. Is it worth throwing my whole tax refund at it or keeping some as cushion?
Our electric bill came in about $80 higher than usual this month. Nothing catastrophic, we just weren't expecting it. I'm trying to figure out if it's the space heater or if the rate went up.
I've been paying the minimum on a store card for a while and just noticed how much of it is interest. Feels dumb that I didn't look sooner. Trying to decide whether to move it to a 0% card.
My partner and I keep going over budget on groceries by maybe a hundred bucks a month. It's not breaking us, but I'd like to get a handle on it before it turns into something bigger.
I missed the due date on my internet bill and got hit with a late fee. That's the second time this year. I have the money, I just lose track of what's due when, and it's starting to cost me.
We had to put the vet bill and a new tire on the credit card in the same week. Now the balance is around $3,000 and I'm not sure how long it'll take me to dig out at the rate I'm going.
My hours got cut from 40 to 32 at work. Rent's still the same. I think I can cover things for a couple months but it's tighter than I'd like and I keep recalculating in my head.
Got a letter saying my student loan payment is going up by $115 a month starting in March. I don't really have $115 spare anywhere. Should I be looking at a different repayment plan?
I'm two months behind on my car payment and the lender keeps calling. I've been letting it go to voicemail because I don't know what to tell them. I get paid Friday but it won't cover both months.
The gas company sent a shutoff notice with a date on it. I can pay part of it but not the whole balance. Do they usually work with you if you call, or does the date just happen?

Between the credit cards and the medical bill from my daughter's ER visit, we're carrying about $14,000 now. My husband and I had a rough conversation about it last night and neither of us has a plan.
I borrowed $2,000 from my mom in the fall and told her I'd pay it back by January. It's March. She hasn't brought it up and that somehow makes it worse. I still don't have it.

We're three months behind on rent. The landlord slipped a notice under the door yesterday saying we have ten days. I have maybe a third of what's owed. I don't know where the kids and I go if this doesn't work.

A collections agency has started calling my work number. My manager said something about it today. I'm scared this turns into a problem with my job on top of everything else, and the job is the only thing holding this together.

My wages are getting garnished starting next paycheck for an old debt I honestly forgot existed. After the garnishment I'm short about $400 a month against my bills. I've run the numbers four times and it doesn't close.

The car got repossessed out of our driveway Tuesday. I need it for work and the bus route takes two hours each way. My wife has stopped talking to me about money entirely and I don't know how to start that conversation again.

The eviction hearing is Thursday. We owe about $7,200 and I have $340. I've called every assistance line in the county and they're all out of funds until July. I keep lying to my son about why we're packing boxes.

I've been hiding the debt from my husband for almost two years. It's around $40,000 across six cards and a personal loan. A default notice came in the mail today and he opens the mail. I feel physically sick.

Power's off, water's scheduled for Friday, and we're staying at my sister's starting tomorrow. I'm 52 and I've never been here before. I don't know how a person comes back from this, honestly. I just need someone to tell me what the next step is.

Foreclosure sale date is set for the 19th. I've been in this house eighteen years. My mom died in the back bedroom. I've stopped opening anything from the bank and I lie awake most nights doing the same math over and over.

I missed the cutoff on my practice driving theory test by two questions. It's only a mock, but I was pretty sure I had it. Retake is Saturday. Any quick way to stop second-guessing myself the whole week?
Didn't pass the first module of my online photography course. It was a portfolio review and they said my compositions were repetitive. Slightly annoying, since I thought that was my strong point.
Failed my typing speed test for a temp job listing. Needed 60 wpm, got 52. Not the end of the world but I've been typing for twenty years, so that stung a bit more than expected.
I auditioned for a small part in the community theatre show and didn't get cast. They said it was close. I'm fine, mostly, just a bit flat today. Is it weird to go to opening night anyway?
Got my results back and I failed the first section of my accounting certification. I studied for about three months around work. Now I have to pay the exam fee again and wait six weeks to retake it.
My final project for the coding bootcamp got marked as not meeting requirements. I have one resubmission left. Feeling pretty stupid about it since I ignored the feedback they gave in week six.
I didn't pass the practical part of my lifeguard recertification. Failed the timed swim. I've been doing this job for four summers and now I'm sitting out until I can book another session.
Second time failing my grade five piano exam. Same piece tripped me up in the same place. My teacher was very kind about it which somehow made it worse. Should I switch pieces entirely?
I failed the bar exam. Not by a huge margin, but failed. Everyone in my study group passed and they're all posting about it. I have to tell my firm on Monday and I don't know how to word it.

Didn't pass my dissertation defense. They gave me a revise-and-resubmit with six months to fix the methodology chapter. Six months I don't really have money for. I've been staring at the same page all evening.

I blew the audition. Forgot the second half of my monologue and just stood there. It was for a company I've wanted to work with since I was nineteen. They were polite about it, which I keep replaying.
My CPA exam results came back failing for the third section. That's two out of four now and the eighteen month clock is running. I'm starting to think I picked the wrong field entirely.
Third and final attempt at my nursing licensure exam and I failed. I'd have to redo coursework to sit it again. Four years of school and I'm not sure I can face starting any part of it over.
The project I've led for two years got cancelled after the review board rejected it. It was my proposal, my design, my team. I have to tell nine people on Monday that their work is going in a drawer.
Failed my flight instructor checkride. The examiner said my judgment wasn't there yet. I've spent about forty thousand on training and I don't have money for more hours. I don't know what I do now.

I didn't make it through my medical board recertification. My hospital privileges are tied to it. I'm fifty-three and I've been practising since I was twenty-eight and I feel like I've been told I'm finished.

Failed my final qualifying exam. My program has terminated my funding and my visa depends on enrollment. Six years of work and I leave the country with nothing. I can't call my parents. I genuinely don't know what happens tomorrow.

The audition was the last one my agent could get me. I choked. She dropped me this morning. I'm thirty-eight, I have no other training, and I've spent my entire adult life on this. I don't know who I am without it.

My final appeal was denied and I'm out of the program permanently. The debt stays. I keep thinking about how everyone at home thinks I'm nearly qualified. I haven't left the flat in three days and I can't stop shaking.

Fifteen years building toward this certification and I failed the last attempt allowed. There is no retake, ever. My whole plan for my family was built on this. I'm sitting in the car in the parking lot and I can't make myself drive home.

I waved back at someone in the grocery store today and they were actually waving at the person behind me. Nobody said anything but I felt my face go hot. Silly, I know, but it's still rattling around in my head an hour later.
I called my coworker by the wrong name in a meeting. Twice. She corrected me the second time and everyone kind of chuckled. Is there a graceful way to bring it up tomorrow or should I just let it go?
Walked around the office for probably two hours with a coffee stain right on the front of my shirt. Nobody mentioned it, which somehow makes it worse. I keep replaying who I talked to.
My camera was on when I thought it was off during the team call. I was eating cereal and making faces at my phone. Someone typed "lol" in the chat. Trying not to think about it.

I mispronounced a client's company name during my part of the presentation and my manager corrected me in front of everyone. It was a small thing but I stumbled through the rest and I've felt off all afternoon.

Found out my team went out for drinks Thursday and I wasn't invited. They talked about it openly at lunch today like I'd obviously know. I don't want to make it a thing, but it stung more than I expected.
I sent a message meant for my friend to the group chat with my in-laws. It wasn't awful, just a bit sarcastic about the weekend plans. Nobody's responded and it's been two hours.

Tripped going up the steps at church with everyone watching and dropped the bulletin everywhere. A couple people helped. I laughed it off but I ended up leaving early. Feeling a bit ridiculous about that.

I gave the wrong numbers in a budget meeting and the finance lead corrected me in front of the whole department. I'd checked them twice. I don't know how I got it that wrong and I can't stop going over it.

My sister-in-law posted photos from a family lunch nobody told me about. My husband's whole side was there. He says it wasn't deliberate. How do I ask about it without sounding like I'm keeping score?
I made a joke at dinner that landed badly and the table went quiet. One person said "okay then" and changed the subject. That was Saturday and I've been avoiding the group chat since.

I got someone's pronouns wrong in front of a room of people and then made it worse by over-apologising. They were gracious about it. I still feel like everyone's opinion of me shifted in that thirty seconds.

I cried in a performance review today. Full on, couldn't stop, had to ask for a minute. Two people walked past the glass door while it was happening. I have to face all of them tomorrow and I don't know how.

I've been at this job eight months and I just realised there's a team lunch every Friday that I've never once been asked to. I found out because someone assumed I was already going. I don't know what I've done.

I stood up to give the toast at my friend's wedding and completely lost my place. Long silence, then I just said congratulations and sat down. Her mother patted my arm. Everyone saw. I want to disappear.

I sent a complaint about my boss to a group thread that included him. He read it. He's said nothing, just scheduled a meeting for Monday and now the whole team knows. Is there anything I can even do before then?

I ran a training session today and had a panic attack halfway through. I had to leave the room in front of forty colleagues. Someone else finished it for me. I've been sitting in my car in the car park since three.

My closest friends organised a weekend away and I only found out from an Instagram story. Ten years of friendship. Nobody has messaged me. I keep opening the chat to say something and closing it again.

I missed a critical step and a patient was harmed. It happened in front of two colleagues and there's an investigation now. Everyone at work knows. I keep seeing their faces when they realised what I'd done.

I got walked out of the building in front of the whole open plan floor today. Security escort, box of my things, everyone watching over their monitors. My badge stopped working before I reached the lift. I haven't told my wife yet.
Someone tried to jimmy the lock on our shed last night. Nothing was taken as far as I can tell, just some scratches on the door. Should I bother reporting it, or is that a waste of everyone's time?
The washing machine hose let go while I was at work and soaked part of the laundry room floor. I've got fans running on it now. Anything I should watch for over the next few days?
A branch came down in the storm and cracked two roof tiles. There's no leak yet but I can see daylight from the attic in one spot. Roofer can't come until next week.
Small grease fire on the stove this evening. I got the lid on it fast and nothing else caught, but the kitchen still smells burnt. Kind of rattled me more than I expected.
Came home to find a window screen cut and the back door standing open. My laptop's gone. Police took a report but said not to get my hopes up. Feeling weirdly unsettled in my own place tonight.
We had about two inches of water in the basement after the rain. Lost some boxes of books and the carpet down there. I'm mopping it out now. Do I need to worry about mold?
Electrical fire in the wall outlet in my bedroom. The fire department caught it early but there's a hole in the drywall and everything smells like smoke. I'm sleeping on the couch for now.
Someone broke into our garage overnight and took my husband's tools. He's had some of those for twenty years. Insurance says it's under our deductible. Not sure what to tell him.
A pipe burst in the ceiling while we were away for the weekend. Water came through into the living room and the floors are buckled. Restoration company says three weeks minimum. We're at my sister's.
Break-in yesterday. They went through every drawer in the house, including the kids' rooms. Took jewelry and cash. I keep checking the locks and I can't seem to settle. Is that normal?

Kitchen fire spread into the cabinets before the fire department got here. Half the room is gone and the rest of the house has smoke damage. We're in a hotel and I'm trying to sort out the insurance claim.
The creek came up faster than anyone expected and we got about a foot through the ground floor. Furniture's ruined, appliances too. Neighbors are all in the same boat. I don't know where to start.

The fire started in the garage overnight. We all got out but the back half of the house is gone and the rest is unlivable. Standing in the driveway this morning looking at it was strange. Not sure what happens next.
Flood took out our whole first floor. Every photo album, my mother's furniture, all of it sitting on the curb now. We're staying with friends and I keep thinking of more things we lost.
They broke in while we were asleep upstairs. Nobody was hurt but they were in the house with us for who knows how long. My daughter won't sleep in her own room. I haven't slept much either.
Structural engineer says the foundation shifted and the back wall isn't safe. We have to move out by the weekend and the repair estimate is more than we paid for the house. Insurance is denying it.
We lost everything in the fire. The house is a shell. I got the kids out and that's all, no documents, no clothes, nothing. I'm sitting in a motel room and I genuinely don't know what to do first.

The water came in at night and we got out through a window. The house is gone, the whole street is gone. Two people down the road didn't make it. I can't stop shaking and nobody can tell me anything yet.
House burned down last week. My husband was in the hospital for smoke inhalation for three days. We had no insurance because I let the policy lapse in the spring. I did this to us.
They kicked the door in while I was home. I hid in the bathroom and heard them going room to room. It's been four days and I still can't be in the house alone. I don't recognize myself right now.
I tripped on the curb walking to the bus this morning and scraped my palm pretty good. It's just a graze but it stings every time I type. Should I keep a bandage on it or let it air out?
Slammed my finger in the car door yesterday. The nail is going a bit purple but I can still bend it fine. Mostly just annoyed at myself for being in a rush.
I stepped wrong coming down the stairs and rolled my ankle a little. It's not swollen, just tender when I push off. I've been icing it on and off. Probably fine to walk the dog tonight?
Burned the inside of my wrist on the oven rack taking out a tray. It's red and a bit shiny but no blister yet. Ran it under cold water for ages. Feels warm still.
I came off my bike on wet leaves Saturday. Nothing broken, but my hip and shoulder are a mess of bruises and I'm stiff getting out of bed. Haven't been back on the bike since.
Cut my thumb chopping onions and ended up getting three stitches at the walk-in clinic. It's healing okay but I keep bumping it and it throbs. Cooking has become weirdly stressful.
I pulled something in my lower back lifting a box of books. Two days later and I still can't sit at my desk for more than twenty minutes. Is it normal for it to be worse on day three?
Slipped in the shower last week and caught the edge of the tub with my ribs. No fracture apparently, just bruised, but sneezing is awful and I'm not sleeping well on that side.

Broke my wrist falling off a ladder while clearing the gutters. I'm in a cast for six weeks and I'm left-handed, so basically everything takes twice as long. Work has been understanding but I feel useless.
I got rear-ended at a light on Tuesday. Car's driveable but my neck has seized up and the physio says whiplash. I keep replaying the sound of it whenever I stop at that intersection.
Tore something in my knee playing football and I'm on crutches until the scan next week. I live on the third floor with no lift. Getting groceries up has become the hardest part of the day.
Dislocated my shoulder at the climbing gym. They popped it back in at A&E but it's in a sling now and I'm told it might happen again. I'm honestly nervous about going back.

I broke my ankle in three places and had surgery with plates and screws two weeks ago. Non-weight-bearing for another eight weeks. I've barely left the sofa and I'm starting to feel like the walls are closing in.
Came off my motorbike on the ring road. Helmet did its job but I've got a fractured collarbone, road rash down one leg, and I can't stop thinking about how close the lorry was behind me.
I fell from a stepladder at work and cracked two vertebrae. Brace for twelve weeks. The doctors say it should heal, but I'm 52 and doing manual work, and I don't know what happens if it doesn't.
Fractured my skull in a fall at a wedding and spent four nights in hospital. I'm home now but the headaches and light sensitivity haven't let up and I can't remember the hour before it happened.
I lost two fingers on my right hand in a table saw accident six weeks ago. The surgeries are done. I'm a carpenter, or I was. I don't know how to think about the rest of it yet.
Head-on collision in November. Six weeks in hospital, pelvis rebuilt, still learning to walk again. Some days I manage. Other days I get panic in the passenger seat and my wife has to pull over.
I fell forty feet on a job site. They didn't expect me to walk and I do, sort of, with a stick and constant pain. Two years on and I still wake up mid-fall most nights.

Burns over my arm, shoulder and part of my face from a kitchen fire in March. Out of the burns unit now, into pressure garments and grafts. I've stopped looking in mirrors and I've cancelled on friends four times.

I moved to Denver about six weeks ago for work. The job's fine, the apartment's fine. I just realized I haven't had a conversation outside of work in like nine days. Is there a normal timeline for this kind of thing?
My college group chat has gotten a lot quieter this year. Nobody's mad, we're all just busy. I keep almost sending something and then not. Feels weird to be the one who always starts it.
I joined a climbing gym mostly to meet people and I've gone eight times without talking to anyone. Everyone seems to already come in pairs. Should I just try a class instead?
Sundays are the strangest day here. I'll do laundry, get groceries, walk around a bit, and by evening I notice I haven't spoken out loud. It's not bad exactly. Just noticeable.

My closest friend from home hasn't answered my last two texts. Not ignoring me, I think, just life. But I've started rereading the thread to see if I said something off. That's probably not a great sign.
Six months in this city and my contacts list is still just coworkers and my landlord. I go to things. I make small talk. It never seems to turn into an actual invitation to anything.

I had a birthday last week and didn't tell anyone here about it. Got some texts from people back home. Spent the evening watching a movie. I keep telling myself it's fine but I've been thinking about it all week.
Everyone I knew in my twenties has paired off or had kids. I'm the one who still texts about getting dinner and gets a rain check. How do you keep asking without feeling like you're bothering people?
I've been here almost a year and I don't think anyone in this city would notice if I disappeared for a week. Not in a dramatic way. Just logistically, nobody's expecting me anywhere.
I stopped reaching out to my old friends to see if any of them would reach out to me first. It's been two months. Nobody has. I don't know what to do with that information.

Work from home, order groceries, gym at odd hours so it's empty. I've built a life where I never have to talk to anyone and now I think I've forgotten how. Conversations feel exhausting in a way they didn't before.
I went to a coworker's party and stood by the snacks for an hour, then left without saying goodbye. Nobody texted. I keep replaying it. I'm starting to think the problem isn't the city.
I talked to a barista today and my voice came out cracked because I hadn't used it since Monday. It's Thursday. I laughed it off but I sat in my car afterward for a while feeling pretty bad about it.
My best friend of fifteen years told me she needed space. That was in March. I've written and deleted maybe forty messages since. I don't know what I did and I don't think I'm going to find out.
I've started keeping the TV on all day just for the voices. I know that's a little sad. It's been two years in this city and I have not made one friend. I'm running out of theories about why.
There's nobody I could call at 2am. Not one person. I did the math on that last night and haven't really been able to shake it since. My family is far and we don't talk like that.

I got sick last month and realized there was literally no one to tell. I lay there for three days and the only person who knew was the delivery driver. I've been feeling hollowed out ever since and I don't know how to say that to anyone.

I think I've become a person nobody thinks about. Everyone from before has moved on and nothing here has taken root. I go whole weeks now feeling like I'm watching my own life from outside it. I don't know how much longer I can do this.

I sat on the floor of my kitchen last night for two hours because I couldn't think of a reason to get up. No one is expecting anything from me. I'm 34 and I've somehow ended up completely alone and I can't see the way back.

Every friendship I've had has just faded out and I'm starting to believe that's about me, not circumstance. Three cities, same pattern. I feel unreachable in a way that scares me and I don't know who I'd even say that to besides this.

My manager mentioned in our one-on-one that she's putting my name forward for the senior title next quarter. Nothing official yet, but she seemed pretty confident. I've been quietly grinning at my desk all afternoon.
I finally got a callback for the second-round interview at the place I actually want to work. It's just a scheduling email but I've read it four times. Any tips for not overpreparing?
My cousin texted that she's flying in for a weekend next month. We haven't seen each other since before she moved abroad. Small thing, but I've been in a good mood since I read it.
Got my routine bloodwork back and everything's in normal range. I wasn't really worried, but I still felt lighter when I saw the results. Planning to take myself out for a decent lunch.

I got the promotion I applied for internally. It's a modest bump in pay but a real change in responsibility. Starts in three weeks. I keep wanting to tell people and then deciding it's not a big enough deal.
My partner and I picked a wedding date this morning. Nothing's booked, no venue, just the date written on the fridge calendar. Feels oddly official. Is it normal to feel this calm about it?
The community college accepted my transfer application. I've been chipping away at prerequisites for two years while working nights, so this actually means something. Classes start in the fall.
My old roommate is back in the country after four years and we're meeting for dinner Thursday. I'm weirdly nervous. We used to talk every day and now I don't know what we'll talk about.
I got the job. Real offer, in writing, better salary than I asked for. I've been unemployed since March and I honestly stopped expecting anything. Signed it an hour ago and I still feel shaky.
My follow-up scan came back clear. Six months of checkups and this was the one I was most worried about. My doctor said we can move to yearly now. I cried in the parking lot, which surprised me.
She said yes. We got engaged last night on a completely ordinary Tuesday walk because I couldn't wait any longer. Her parents already know somehow. I haven't slept much.
I got into the graduate program. Full funding, the one I thought was a long shot. Third time applying. I read the email standing in my kitchen and just sat down on the floor.

My dad's oncologist used the word remission today. After eighteen months of scans and treatments and me flying back and forth every other weekend. He made a joke on the drive home. I'd forgotten what that sounded like.
I found my birth mother. We've been emailing for two weeks and we're meeting in person on Saturday. Thirty-four years. I don't know what to bring or what to say or how to be normal about this.
They made me a partner at the firm. I've been there eleven years and I stopped believing it was going to happen around year eight. My wife cried. I mostly just feel stunned and very tired.
After four rounds of IVF, the test came back positive and the first scan looked good. We haven't told anyone. I'm scared to be happy but I also can't stop being happy. Does that make sense?

My son walked across the stage this morning. Six years ago the doctors told us he might never speak in full sentences. He gave a speech. I don't know how to describe what happened in my chest when he started talking.
I got the all-clear. Final scan, no evidence of disease, treatment is done. Two years of my life. I'm sitting in my car in the hospital lot and I can't make myself drive home yet.

My brother came home yesterday after seven years of no contact. He knocked on the door and my mother didn't recognize him for a second. We stayed up until four in the morning. I still don't fully believe it.

The adoption was finalized this morning. She's been with us for two years and today a judge said she's ours permanently. She asked if she could change her middle name to match mine. I'm not functioning today.
I have a second-round interview on Thursday. It's for a role I'd like but wouldn't be crushed to lose. Any suggestions for what to prep beyond the usual questions?
Got a five-minute update to present at our team meeting Monday. I've done these before, just want it to sound less like I'm reading off a slide.
Flying to Denver next week. I'm a slightly nervous flyer, nothing serious, but I always sleep badly the night before. Wondering if that's just normal.
Minor foot surgery scheduled for the 12th. Outpatient, home the same day. I keep catching myself thinking about it at odd moments even though everyone says it's routine.
Interview tomorrow morning at nine. I've been rehearsing answers in the shower and while driving. Part of me wants to cancel and pretend I never applied.
I have to give a toast at my cousin's wedding in three weeks. I've written four versions and hated all of them. My hands shake when I even practice out loud.
Knee surgery is booked for the 20th. It's my first time under general anesthesia and that part bothers me more than the actual procedure does. Is that a common thing?
Six-hour flight on Saturday and I've been checking turbulence forecasts every day this week. I know that's not helping but I keep doing it anyway.
Final interview on Friday for a job I really need. My current contract ends in six weeks. I've been waking up at four in the morning running through it in my head.
I'm presenting to about eighty people at a conference next month. I've turned down two smaller talks already to avoid this feeling. Now I can't back out of this one.
Gallbladder surgery next Wednesday. My mom had a bad reaction to anesthesia years ago and I can't stop thinking about that. I haven't told anyone I'm this worried about it.
I fly to my sister's wedding in nine days and I've been dreading it since the invitation came. Chest gets tight just picturing boarding. Is there anything that actually helps in the moment?
Interview Monday. I've been unemployed eleven months and this is the first real callback. I feel sick every time I look at the calendar. Not sure I'll be able to eat that morning.
I have to defend my thesis in front of the committee on the 8th. I've frozen in front of a room before and it still comes back to me. My stomach has been off for days.
Surgery is Tuesday and they mentioned a small chance they'll need to do more than planned once they're in there. I've read the consent form maybe fifteen times now. I can't settle.
I have a flight in four days that I can't get out of, work is paying, and I've already cried about it twice. Last time I flew I gripped the armrest the whole way and couldn't speak.

My surgery is Thursday morning. It's bigger than anything I've had before and I've spent the last two nights lying awake thinking about what happens if something goes wrong. I wrote my passwords down for my partner just in case.

The interview is tomorrow and it's the difference between keeping my apartment and moving back in with my parents at forty. I've been shaking on and off all evening and I can't get my thoughts in order.

I'm supposed to speak at my father's memorial on Saturday in front of everyone he knew. I've tried reading it aloud three times and couldn't get past the second line without breaking down. I don't know how I'm going to stand up there.

Flight is in eleven hours and I haven't slept at all. I'm sitting on the bathroom floor with my heart going. I know statistically it's fine, I know all of it, and none of it is touching this right now.
